chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn A'yan al-Bazzaz, who reported from Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Sabeeh, who reported from Khalaf ibn Khalifa, from Sa'id ibn Ubaid al-Ta'i, from Ali ibn Rabi'a al-Walibi, from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"Indeed, Allah the Exalted has set limits for you, so do not transgress them; and has made certain acts obligatory upon you, so do not waste them; and has set traditions for you, so follow them; and has made sacred certain sanctities, so do not desecrate them; and He has pardoned you regarding certain matters as a mercy from Him for you, without forgetting them, so do not burden yourselves with them."

key_terms.تتكلفوها: Do not burden yourselves - regarding matters God has pardoned
key_terms.حدود: Hudud - Divine limits and boundaries set by God that must not be transgressed
key_terms.حرمات: Hurumat - Sacred sanctities and prohibitions that must not be violated
key_terms.سنن: Sunan - Established traditions and practices to be followed
key_terms.فرائض: Fara'id - Obligatory religious duties prescribed by God

ai.seo_question: What are the five categories of divine legislation in Islam according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), as narrated through Imam Ali (AS), outlines five categories of divine legislation: limits (hudud), obligations (fara'id), traditions (sunan), sacred prohibitions (hurumat), and pardoned matters. This comprehensive framework was addressed to the Muslim community to clarify the scope and boundaries of religious law, emphasizing that divine silence on certain matters is deliberate mercy, not oversight.
